commands.authority: repository-v6 atomic exact Git admission or native unborn authority
acceptance_spec: fresh Git repositories import the complete exact reachable object, ref, change, tree, mode, symlink, gitlink, and non-code-artifact closure atomically
fresh non-Git repositories create only an unborn repository-v6 authority
existing .kin and non-empty non-Git directories fail without mutation
safe exact Git remote mappings are sealed into graph-adjacent local transport config while unsafe mappings fail closed before .kin publication
a Git worktree carrying uncommitted work is admitted at its committed state, with every differing path disclosed in human and JSON output rather than refused

either boundary adopts an existing repository's identity when asked to, so a store created here can publish into a repository that already holds one, and refuses an identity the local store cannot be keyed by before a layout is staged
commands.note: The clean-slate admission dispatcher is implemented and covered by exact Git and native-unborn acceptance tests. Repository authority is the committed workspace seed and nothing else, so index and worktree state that is not the seed is observed and reported rather than refused: it stays in the worktree and the daemon admits it as workspace state through the same seam it admits every later edit. What still refuses is ambiguity about the source itself, where the committed state a migration would seal is not decidable, which is an in-progress Git operation, a conflicted or sparse index, an entry Git has been told not to compare, a materialized nested repository, a hook the repository owns, a checkout filter, another registered worktree that anchors commits the shared reference store does not name or still has an operation running against the object database, and repository-local transport configuration outside the safe exact subset. That last refusal now names every offending key rather than the first, and admits the keys it has classified as unable to affect transport. Init also adopts an existing repository's identity when `--adopt-repository-id` names one, on the Git boundary and the native boundary both. It exists because every exact-transfer surface is identity-exact and none can be retargeted after the fact: building a segment refuses a source authority whose repository differs from the destination's, and pack validation refuses a pack whose alias records name another repository, so a store meant to publish into a repository that already exists has to carry that identity from the moment it is created. A minted identity is still a UUID v4, which is what keeps two independently created repositories from colliding; an adopted one may be any identity the local store can be keyed by, which for a store laid out at `{base}/{repo_id}/` means one portable filesystem component, refused before a layout is staged. What this does NOT reach is a hosted repository holding real content: a Git-admitted store adopting a hosted identity still meets transfer v1's imported-Git authority bound, measured and recorded rather than inferred.

commands.authority: repository-v6 workspace/ref/root bundle
acceptance_spec: report one coherent durable authority generation, exact workspace head/tree, dirty state, refs, and semantic-enrichment state
do not infer repository membership or readiness from the filesystem or legacy branch sidecars
commands.note: Status reads workspace, refs, roots, exact tree identity, and semantic counts from one repository authority lease; checkout and Git state are not consulted.

commands.authority: sealed exact-workspace observation consumed by repository-v6 transaction and compare-and-swap ref publication
acceptance_spec: retain a non-fabricable complete workspace observation and its directory capabilities through final authority publication
bind the observed path manifest, exact admission policy, source CAS closure, prior tree, roots, and generation into one commit transaction without replanning against newer authority
reject an unconfirmed mass deletion as a whole observation without publishing simultaneous additions, modifications, policy changes, or graph state
commit exact workspace tree deltas and semantic deltas in one repository transaction
preserve all unsupported-language and non-code artifacts, modes, symlinks, gitlinks, and byte-exact paths
publish the target ref with generation and root-bundle compare-and-swap and no raw-filesystem rebuild
commands.note: Commit consumes one complete host observation that carries the scanner's completion proof into publication, binds the observed manifest to the authority roots and prior workspace tree it was planned against, and refuses rather than replans when authority moved. An unconfirmed mass deletion refuses the whole observation, so no addition, modification, or derived admission-policy state published beside it.

commands.authority: repository-v6 workspace/ref plus immutable change DAG
acceptance_spec: resolve the active workspace head through exact repository refs and external aliases
walk immutable semantic parents without legacy branch state or Git/filesystem fallback
commands.note: Log resolves one exact workspace base and walks the immutable change DAG from one repository-v6 lease; Git, checkout files, and legacy branch state are not consulted.

commands.authority: immutable repository-v6 trees and semantic changes
acceptance_spec: diff exact tree membership, byte paths, content identities, executable bits, symlinks, and gitlinks as well as semantic entity and relation changes
resolve omitted endpoints from repository-v6 workspace/ref authority
commands.note: Diff resolves refs, changes, Git aliases, HEAD, and the graph-owned workspace from one authority lease; exact byte-path artifact transitions remain complete when semantic enrichment is absent.

commands.authority: repository-v6 byte-exact refs
acceptance_spec: list full byte-exact refs and identify the workspace symbolic or detached head from one authority generation
commands.note: Branch list reads canonical fully-qualified byte refs, targets, default ref, and active workspace head from one repository-v6 authority lease.

commands.authority: repository-v6 ref transaction
acceptance_spec: create a fully qualified ref with MustNotExist compare-and-swap against the active workspace base target
commands.note: Branch creation commits MustNotExist against the exact active workspace base target and repository root bundle.

commands.authority: repository-v6 ref transaction
acceptance_spec: delete an exact ref only with force-with-lease and reject deletion of the active symbolic head
commands.note: Branch deletion commits force-with-lease against the exact target and rejects default or checked-out refs.

commands.authority: repository-v6 workspace transaction and graph-derived projection
acceptance_spec: transition exact workspace head and tree atomically against expected generation and roots
verify every blob and symlink body from repository CAS while materializing only entries this host can represent
retain complete graph authority across Gitlink add, remove, and retarget operations and host-unrepresentable byte paths without inventing source blobs
preserve independently owned Gitlink directories without traversing their contents and fail closed on namespace races or projection tampering
commands.note: Branch switch resolves byte-exact repository refs from one authority lease, verifies the complete blob and symlink closure from repository CAS, and commits the exact workspace mutation through a crash-recoverable projection WAL. Gitlinks and host-unrepresentable paths remain exact graph members; only host-materializable source bodies are projected.

commands.authority: repository-v6 exact external objects, refs, aliases, and source CAS
acceptance_spec: rehydrate an exact Git repository from repository authority without synthesizing or rewriting imported objects
export native Kin changes deterministically with refs updated only after object closure verification
commands.note: On Unix, Git export captures one repository-v6 authority lease, loads exact source and imported object bodies only from repository CAS, self-verifies staged refs and HEAD, and publishes only to a new external destination through a retained parent capability. Other hosts fail before creating the export.

commands.authority: repository-v6 workspace tree and source CAS
acceptance_spec: verify every projected path, kind, mode, symlink target, and blob against one durable workspace generation
stop graph projection, freeze the same authority roots, and atomically detach the locked .kin namespace only after exact replacement Git is durable
restore only the credential-free Git remote, tracking, refspec, and push configuration sealed during exact admission
retain detached Kin authority and any previous Git directory in a recoverable sibling archive; recursive purge is not an eject product surface
commands.note: On Unix, eject proves the complete graph-owned workspace against repository source CAS, durably builds and fsck-verifies a replacement ordinary Git repository, restores sealed safe Git interoperability config, then holds projection and authority freezes through one capability-anchored Git replacement and .kin detach transaction. Windows currently fails before namespace mutation.

commands.authority: native repository-v6 replica bootstrap or exact Git transport followed by atomic admission
acceptance_spec: clone with Git transport into an empty destination and call the same exact kin init admission boundary
remove a Git transport destination created by this invocation when exact Git admission fails
negotiate native repository identity and declared default branch before initializing the destination
commit native or imported Git history, immutable bodies and the initial workspace together against generation-zero roots, then publish the complete projected clone without replacement
clone an empty native repository without inventing history and pull its first later commit through saved origin
retain repository identity and saved origin for ordinary pull retry after daemon startup failure
reject occupied or symlink destinations without clobber and reject invalid bootstrap bodies or identity before destination publication
support a native commit and ordinary push from the cloned client, then recover exact bytes and history in another fresh clone
commands.note: The CLI accepts hosted native locators or an HTTP peer with --repository. It adopts the verified repository identity, creates a distinct workspace, and persists a credential-free native origin. Initial history and workspace authority are committed together in private staging, with exact bodies projected before no-replace publication. Native artifact introductions, edits, imported Git history, empty native repositories and saved-origin push/pull are exercised through real daemons. A source advancing after the first advertisement is cloned at the subsequently transferred head. Clone follows the declared default branch. Imported Git bootstrap still has to fit one negotiated pack. A gitlink or another source entry this host cannot materialize is refused before target publication. Hosted service protection rules have separate acceptance.

commands.authority: atomic repository-v6 exact Git admission
acceptance_spec: in-place migration calls the same exact Git admission boundary as init
snapshot or partial-history modes are rejected
commands.note: The migration executor is a thin exact-admission wrapper.

commands.authority: daemon-private repository-v6 exact tree, semantic graph, source CAS, and crash-recoverable projection transaction
acceptance_spec: resolve a selected immutable change through startup-pinned repository and workspace identity without Git or legacy object fallback
refuse a repository storage namespace replaced at the same ambient path, detached, or absent from the pinned store instead of answering from replacement authority
verify complete selected tree, semantic graph, and source CAS closure before one projection and authority transaction

preserve every unsupported-language and non-code artifact, executable bit, symlink, gitlink, opaque binary, and host-unrepresentable byte path in graph authority while materializing only host-representable entries
reject every session-scoped request before mutation and preserve independently dirty unselected paths
replay the exact caller-stable operation across same-daemon and restart crash gaps without advancing authority twice
commands.note: Checkout binds only the repository and workspace identity this daemon pinned at startup, revalidates the retained per-repository storage namespace before planning, and answers a namespace replaced at the same ambient path, detached, or absent from the pinned store with a typed conflict instead of mismatched truth. Exact projection, universal artifact preservation, and caller-stable replay are proven across same-daemon and restart gaps. The retained-identity refusals are proven on Unix; the Windows file-identity path is implemented but not covered by CI.

commands.authority: repository-v6 remote capability and exact transport
acceptance_spec: negotiate the remote destination lease, build the exact closure, publish it, and verify the returned receipt binds the pack that was sent
refuse a non-fast-forward gap with both heads named and no force path
carry a closure larger than one negotiated envelope as an ordered sequence of packs, each published in its own repository transaction and proven by its own receipt
leave an interrupted multi-pack publication on the last head that was receipted, which is an exact ancestor of the target, and resume from there on a re-run
refuse a step that cannot be split, naming the negotiated bound it exceeds, whether that step is one change or the smallest one a merge leaves reachable

publish into a replica that has admitted nothing by establishing the publisher's imported-Git authority in the same transaction as the history it describes, refusing a destination that is not unborn and refusing a bootstrap too large for one pack, and doing all of it with no operator interaction so a headless caller drives it unattended
publish native artifact introductions under the receiving replica's shared admission policy, including an ordinary saved-origin push from a cloned client
commands.note: Push negotiates exact destination authority and verifies every returned receipt. Native introductions, edits and removals use the receiver's shared admission policy. A real cloned client commits a new binary artifact and pushes through saved origin; another fresh clone verifies its bytes, tree and history from the receiving peer. Native continuation packs resume from the last receipted head. Imported Git authority can be established only on a generation-zero destination with no history or default ref and its bootstrap must fit one negotiated pack. Existing incompatible imported Git authority and non-fast-forward histories are refused. Gitlinks remain authenticated against imported Git authority. The exercised peer is the Kin daemon transfer seam; hosted service protection rules have separate acceptance.

commands.authority: repository-v6 remote capability and exact transport
acceptance_spec: read the remote ref advertisement, adopt its default ref when this replica has none, and fetch the exact exported closure
admit each pack in one local authority transaction and refuse a receipt that does not bind it
refuse a remote this replica already contains, naming the remote head
carry a closure larger than one negotiated envelope as an ordered sequence of packs, resuming from the last one admitted
report a derived-view refresh that fails after authority is durable as a typed partial success rather than a server error
transition the graph-derived workspace onto the admitted head through the same projection transaction a branch switch commits, so the working tree shows what was pulled
report a working tree that could not follow, naming what blocked it, without revoking the history that is already durable

plan no workspace transition for a pull that admitted no history, and still answer whether the working tree stands at the ref by comparing the workspace's recorded base target against the ref's current target, so an ordinary no-op pull exits clean while a retry over a tree an earlier pull left behind reports it behind and exits non-zero
pull new native artifacts and edits through the origin persisted by native clone, including the first commit after an empty clone
commands.note: Pull admits exact history and bodies per pack, then moves the graph-derived workspace onto the final received ref through the existing projection transaction. Native artifact introductions use the receiver's shared admission policy. Real cloned clients pull edits and new paths through saved origin, including a first commit after empty clone and a native addition after Git import. An incompatible repository identity or non-fast-forward history is refused. A workspace with uncommitted state or externally edited tracked files stays behind and reports a nonzero result while received history remains durable. A no-op pull verifies whether the workspace already follows its ref. If an earlier transfer received all history but left the workspace behind, branch switch completes that remaining projection. Imported Git bootstrap has the same unborn-destination and one-pack bounds as push. Hosted service protection rules have separate acceptance.

commands.authority: repository-v6 immutable DAG three-way composition published with ref compare-and-swap
acceptance_spec: resolve both heads and their merge base by replaying the change DAG, never from raw files
compose semantic entities, relations, and exact tree artifacts by stable identity against the merge base
author the merge change against its first parent and record both heads as ordered parents
publish the merge change, the target ref, and the exact workspace in one repository transaction with compare-and-swap
park a merge that does not compose as one durable merge-transaction record without publishing any part of it
refuse an unrelated, criss-cross, or admission-policy-changing merge without publishing any part of it
commands.note: Merge composes graph truth: both heads and the single merge base are materialized by DAG replay, then entities, relations, and exact tree artifacts are merged by stable identity against that base. Composition decides each identity by whole value, so a side that did not move never overrides a side that did, and both sides moving differently is a conflict rather than a resolution. Granularity is the whole entity or artifact, never the line. Two branches editing disjoint regions of one file therefore conflict, because a semantic-entity model has no textual line merge to fall back on. A move on one branch against an edit on the other conflicts as well, because an artifact's path is part of the value being compared and history that records the move as a removal plus an addition leaves the edited side conflicting against that removal. The merge change carries ordered parents with the active branch first and its deltas are authored against that first parent, which is what history replay validates. Up-to-date and fast-forward merges publish no merge change. A merge that does not compose is now parked rather than refused: the conflict set is published as one durable merge-transaction record bound to the workspace, no ref moves, and the workspace stays at the restore point the record captures, so `kin conflicts` and `kin resolve` continue it. Shapes that are still not proven fail closed with nothing published and are named in the refusal: unrelated histories; multiple merge bases (criss-cross); a merge that would change the shared admission policy; a dirty or detached workspace; and a second merge on a workspace whose merge is already in progress. One interaction is inherited, not introduced: a workspace whose semantics were installed from history (branch switch, checkout, or merge) and is then committed retains a semantic overlay, because the commit observation re-derives entities from source bytes while the installed ones came from replayed history. `kin branch switch` followed by `kin commit` reproduces it with no merge involved.

commands.authority: repository-v6 workspace transaction
acceptance_spec: persist and restore exact graph-owned workspace state without branch sidecars or raw-file inference
commands.note: Sealing writes the exact workspace tree and base-relative semantics as one immutable change under refs/kin/stash/, and restore refuses a moved authority base rather than rebasing onto it. The live-daemon wedge that held this gate closed is fixed: the daemon query graph is a derived view that runs ahead of workspace authority because reconciliation and asynchronous LSP enrichment publish into it continuously, so commands now plan their daemon-side transition from the live graph, and a commit publishes an entity whose provenance moved even when its fingerprint did not. Against a live daemon a seal now returns a clean workspace, restore succeeds, and the freshness-gated commands that follow either half of the cycle succeed rather than refusing until the daemon reopens.

commands.authority: sealed exact-session observation consumed by repository-v6 explicit ingestion boundary
acceptance_spec: retain the session root capability and a non-fabricable observation seal through final namespace revalidation and authority commit
bind exact policy, exclusions, complete source CAS closure, prior roots, and generation into the consumed observation
reject an unconfirmed mass deletion atomically without admitting simultaneous additions or modifications
admit an explicitly observed projection delta into exact workspace authority with complete artifact identities and source CAS
never answer semantic queries or silently repair authority from raw files
commands.note: The session scanner performs retained-root double observation and authority-root CAS, and its observation now owns the retained no-follow directory capability it was taken through. Every field is private, so the observation cannot be built outside the scanner, and planning re-proves the retained capability before anything is planned against it.

commands.authority: repository-v6 authority transition published through the daemon's own complete exact-tree admission seam
acceptance_spec: run the same complete exact-tree admission the watch loop and commit run, rather than a second admission implementation that could admit differently
hold a registered daemon session for the duration so the idle window cannot end the pass in flight, and release it on every exit path
report the outcome from the reconcile probes rather than from the request succeeding, because a pass can fail inside a request that returns cleanly
exit nonzero on a failed pass, leading with the recorded cause and stating that graph authority is unchanged
commands.note: The daemon admits a complete exact tree on startup, on commit, and on what its watcher observed, and none of those is a trigger an operator can pull, so a graph that fell behind its working tree waits for churn that may not come while a quiet daemon idles out first. This command is that trigger. It runs the daemon's own admission seam, so it inherits the same completion proof, authority compare-and-swap, and mass-deletion guard, and it carries no mass-deletion override of its own because the guard's override is read from the daemon's environment and a second control over one guard is two rules that can disagree.

commands.authority: repository-v6 authority transition published through the daemon coordination gate
acceptance_spec: report the tracked paths current ignore rules cover without changing anything unless --confirm is given
publish the retirement as one authority transition, holding the coordination gate so the watch loop cannot admit a competing observation between the reported set and the published change
evict the entities, layout, and index presence derived from a retired path so it stops ranking, leaving the file on disk
refuse a purge that removes more than 75% of a non-trivial tree unless --confirm-mass-deletion accepts it
commands.note: Admission retracts a tracked path once the rules cover it, so this exists for the operator who wants to see the covered set before the next observation clears it, or to retire it now. The default is a dry run naming counts and a bounded path sample. A confirmed purge plans from a complete working-directory walk and reports what the transition did rather than what was planned, because that walk can also carry an edit made since the last watch-loop tick.

commands.authority: repository-v6 durable merge-transaction record
acceptance_spec: read conflict state committed with the exact merge transaction rather than a .kin sidecar
represent semantic and exact-tree conflicts across every artifact kind
recover the exact workspace-bound record across a daemon restart
commands.note: The conflict set is the durable merge-transaction record repository authority holds for this workspace, not a rendering of one and not the retired sidecar shape (.kin/merge_state.json). Every entry carries its subject by stable identity, why it failed to compose, a content digest of the base, ours, and theirs values, and how it has been settled if it has. The record is rooted in local authority, so it survives a daemon restart and is excluded from replicated truth. A terminated record is still returned as the durable account of the last merge on the workspace, so whether a merge is in progress is a state check rather than an existence check. The listing reports the record identity, which `kin resolve --expect` requires to still be current.

commands.authority: repository-v6 merge resolution transaction
acceptance_spec: resolve semantic and exact-tree conflicts against one durable merge transaction
publish the resolved workspace and target ref atomically with compare-and-swap
refuse a resolution authored against a merge record another session has advanced
abort by proving the workspace equals the recorded restore point and moving no ref
commands.note: Resolution moves the durable merge-transaction record through the sealed repository transaction path. Settling entries and publishing the merge are separate transactions by construction: a record commits the resolutions it already carries, so the transaction that publishes never decides any part of the merge. Each settlement carries its actor, timestamp, and the operation that committed it, and the persistence layer proves that operation is the one committing it, so provenance cannot name a transaction that never happened. `--expect` binds a resolution to the record identity the caller read, so a session resolving against a view another session already advanced is refused rather than silently rebased. Completing recomposes from graph truth and holds the result to the record: same identities, same divergences, same side digests, or the merge fails loud rather than publishing a different merge than the one resolved. A resolution that claims a side is checked against history rather than trusted. The merge change, the target ref by compare-and-swap against the recorded first parent, the exact workspace, and the record's termination publish in one transaction. Aborting proves the workspace still equals the recorded restore point and terminates the record without moving any ref. Authoring a resolution value neither side holds is not a proven shape and is refused; every divergence the composer produces is settled by taking a side, removing the identity, or naming which claimant keeps a contested path.

commands.authority: graph entity identity plus repository-v6 source CAS
acceptance_spec: plan edits from graph relations and immutable repository source bodies only
require positive versioned graph extraction coverage plus repository-wide source-CAS occurrence accounting for every declaration and reference site
refuse named-import and qualified-name cases whose graph evidence cannot prove every source token
apply exact workspace tree and semantic deltas through one repository transaction
commands.note: Rename is enabled only for bounded exact cases whose graph and repository source CAS can prove exhaustive. It is not a claim of fully general all-language refactoring: named imports and qualified declarations without exact occurrence evidence still refuse. Every source must carry a positive versioned full-extraction certificate with no incomplete certificate, then a repository-wide Unicode-safe occurrence census must match declarations and rename-relevant graph edges exactly; comments, strings, hidden dynamic references, count mismatches, overlap, missing layouts, shallow or partial coverage, unsupported lexical forms, cross-file new-name collisions, and unowned occurrences fail closed. Cursor lines are converted once from the CLI's 1-based domain to graph 0-based rows, columns are explicit UTF-8 byte offsets with exclusive span ends, and reference cursors cannot select an unrelated same-named declaration. Changed bodies are reparsed in memory; the renamed declaration retains its graph identity; relation identity topology remains unchanged; and the exact tree, semantic delta, native change, workspace, and branch publish through one compare-and-swap transaction guarded by the projection recovery journal. Durable metadata binds the caller request to the canonical identity, original report, and edit set so immediate, restart, qualified-selector, response-loss, and post-later-generation replays return the same committed outcome without reinstalling old authority.

commands.authority: repository-v6 workspace/ref state and negotiated remote capability
acceptance_spec: derive the local publication head from one repository authority generation
read the remote destination lease over the repository-v6 transfer seam and classify the gap without moving history
refuse a remote head this replica has not admitted, naming both heads, with no force path
refuse the imported-Git baseline and the missing or mismatched source bodies a push would refuse, before anything is published
report how many packs the publication will take at the negotiated envelope
commands.note: Negotiates against a live peer transfer seam and publishes nothing. Everything a push decides before it ships bytes is decided here too: the lease, the fast-forward classification, the imported-Git baseline, and the presence and identity of every immutable body the publication head's tree depends on. The per-pack byte arithmetic is only knowable once packs are assembled, so the plan reports the pack count and the negotiated bound rather than predicting that refusal.

commands.authority: repository-v6 CAS session projection admitted through the explicit reconcile boundary
acceptance_spec: materialize a bounded exact workspace snapshot from repository CAS
capture session deltas back through explicit repository transactions or discard them
commands.note: The daemon materializes repository CAS bodies into a disposable .kin/runs/session-<id> projection, the command runs with its working directory inside it, and a clean exit admits the observed delta through the same reconcile boundary `kin reconcile` uses. A non-zero exit keeps the projection instead of admitting or deleting it, --discard removes it without touching authority, and --keep defers admission. Any projection kept this way is collected by the `kin reconcile <session>` that admits it, and stays on disk if that reconcile is refused. Argument boundaries are preserved unless --shell is given. Scoped sessions stay fail-closed.

commands.authority: repository-v6 CAS session projection admitted through the explicit reconcile boundary
acceptance_spec: open an editor over an exact graph-derived workspace with stable artifact identity
retain non-code files, unsupported languages, modes, symlinks, and gitlinks
commands.note: Launches code or cursor over a session projection carrying every host-representable artifact at its repository identity, with executable modes and symlinks intact and gitlinks plus host-unrepresentable members preserved graph-only. Editors detach from the launching process, so the projection is retained and admitted explicitly with `kin reconcile <session>` rather than on an exit that never arrives. Admission is also the collector: a successful `kin reconcile` removes the projection it just took, and a refused one leaves it on disk, so a retained projection lives exactly until its changes land. The discontinued native-fork restriction flags are fail-closed.

commands.authority: repository-v6 CAS session projection plus a capability-scoped daemon session lease
acceptance_spec: bind the assistant to an exact repository generation and capability-scoped session
capture or discard complete exact deltas without hidden working-tree authority
commands.note: Launches claude, codex, or gemini inside a session projection pinned to the repository generation its base records, under a daemon session lease with declared capabilities that the assistant's MCP calls bind to through KIN_SESSION_ID. A clean exit admits the complete observed delta through reconcile and releases the lease; the assistant never writes through the owning working tree. The lease is registered with the launcher PID, so an assistant that dies is reaped on the PID liveness check rather than waiting out the idle window. The 1800 second idle window is the release path for sessions registered without a PID, which now hold their hard-lock scopes against other sessions for up to that long instead of the previous 60 seconds; the sweeper is their only collector, and KIN_SESSION_IDLE_TTL_SECS lowers the window for deployments that would rather take the mid-task reaping risk. Any local process holding a session id can refresh that lease, which the loopback-only bind is the boundary for. Prompt-guidance injection, --session, and the native-fork restriction flags are fail-closed.

commands.authority: repository-v6 CAS session projection admitted through the explicit reconcile boundary
acceptance_spec: start a shell in an exact graph-derived workspace
capture or discard complete exact deltas through repository authority
commands.note: Starts $SHELL with its working directory inside a session projection materialized from repository CAS. Exiting the shell admits the observed delta through the reconcile boundary and removes the projection; a non-zero exit keeps it for `kin reconcile <session>`. The discontinued native-fork restriction flags are fail-closed.

commands.authority: repository-v6 exact workspace tree and graph-owned member content
acceptance_spec: compare a bounded projection observation against one exact workspace generation
load every compared member's content from repository authority and never from the working copy
read only paths the exact workspace tree already tracks
refuse the report when repository authority cannot be opened or moves under the observation
commands.note: Drift compares the derived projection against the exact workspace tree and the member content repository authority owns. The observation is pinned to one authority generation and workspace generation and is refused rather than reported when either moves, so a drift result always describes one exact workspace state. Untracked host paths are never read and never reported: they are not graph-owned, so they cannot drift. Healing is a separate gate.

commands.authority: repository-v6 exact checkout transactions over the diverged paths a drift observation named
acceptance_spec: restore every path a drift observation named, each under the exact repository checkout transaction that already publishes its workspace mutation
select restore targets from byte-exact repository paths the daemon reported, never by parsing them back out of a human message
refuse rather than heal when the report names a divergence count it did not name paths for
re-observe drift after restoring and fail unless the projection is proved clean
commands.note: Heal is the write half of --drift and owns no authority of its own. It observes drift through the daemon, restores each diverged path through the same exact checkout transaction `kin checkout <path>` publishes, and then re-observes, failing unless the projection is proved clean. This is deliberately weaker than one retained whole-workspace freeze: RepoPath still cannot name the whole workspace, so a heal is a sequence of per-path transactions rather than one atomic rematerialization. The closing observation is what proves the end state, so a partial heal reports the remainder instead of reading as success. Nothing pins the authority generation across the sequence, because CheckoutRequest carries none, so authority that moves mid-heal is caught by that closing observation rather than refused as it happens. Heal restores graph-owned content over the working file, which DISCARDS uncommitted changes to any tracked file that diverges; it is not a merge and there is no undo.

commands.authority: repository-v6 immutable change DAG
acceptance_spec: derive API impact from repository-v6 changes at explicit refs without legacy branches
classify impact from entity visibility, role, and declaration fingerprints alone
refuse an endpoint repository authority cannot resolve
commands.note: Impact is a function of the entities repository authority owns at two explicitly named endpoints, resolved through the same exact endpoint resolver diff uses (ref, change, Git object, HEAD, or WORKSPACE). Both endpoints must be named: there is no branch-shape or commit-message inference and no working-copy scan. The published surface is public, source-role, non-container entities; removal, a changed declaration fingerprint, and unpublishing are breaking, new and newly published surface is additive, and a changed behavior fingerprint behind a stable declaration is a patch.

commands.authority: repository-v6 refs, proof state, and immutable tree
acceptance_spec: bind the release snapshot to exact repository roots, proof decisions, and immutable artifacts
publish the snapshot through the same tag ref transaction it describes
seal the binding under a digest that changes with any bound component
commands.note: A release snapshot is the tag transaction plus the exact state it names: the roots the transaction moved between, the change it points at, the content hash and artifact composition of the complete immutable tree, the entity and relation counts, and the policy decision that admitted it. All of it is sealed under one digest, so a snapshot that reports a different tree, source, or policy outcome is a different snapshot. It is not a separate authority path: the same refs/tags/ compare-and-swap and the same release policy that gate `kin tag` gate this.

commands.authority: repository-v6 tag ref transaction
acceptance_spec: create an exact refs/tags target with compare-and-swap and proof-policy checks
decide release policy over the same authority lease the compare-and-swap carries
publish nothing when any declared policy check fails
refuse to move or replace an existing tag ref
commands.note: A tag is a refs/tags/ MustNotExist compare-and-swap in one repository transaction against the exact workspace base target. Release policy is decided over the same authority lease the transaction carries as its expected roots, so the source that was checked and the source that is published are the same immutable state, and an authority move between them refuses the publication instead of tagging an unchecked source. Declared policy is enforced and never downgraded to a warning: --require-proof fails closed for every non-empty source because VerificationRun still carries no immutable source binding, --require-approval fails closed on any unapproved reachable non-root change, and a source below the baseline coverage ratio requires --force to record an explicit acknowledgment in the receipt.

commands.note: Rollback moves history forward. It derives the transition by comparing two immutable graph states, then publishes one new change whose content is exactly the restored change's content, so the change being undone stays in history and every restored artifact keeps the identity and source CAS entry it already had. The change, the branch compare-and-swap, and the workspace transition are one repository transaction committed with the projection, so the repository is never observable at a tree no ref names. Restoring a change outside this branch's history, rolling back over graph-owned uncommitted state, or rolling back over a diverged projection are refusals. Rolling back every change linked to a work item (--feature) is not implemented and refuses.
